title: Beat licences and split sheets — general guidance
content: Beat sales and free downloads are governed by licence terms covering exclusivity, streams, credit, and resale. Without a written licence, disputes turn on messages and payment proof. Always use split sheets naming beatmakers, writers, and percentage shares. Keep licences and payment records.

title: Music collective management (MCSK, KAMP, PRISK) — general guidance
content: Kenyan music rights are administered through licensed collective management organisations for authors, producers, and performers. Registration and membership affect royalty collection. Keep membership records, work declarations, and royalty statements.

title: Copyright Act, 2001 — overview
content: The Copyright Act protects original literary, musical, artistic, and audio-visual works, including beats, songs, and recordings, against unauthorised reproduction and distribution. Protection arises on creation, but registration helps prove ownership. Keep project files, dated exports, and registration certificates.

title: Actor and crew contracts
content: Production contracts state roles, pay, hours, image rights, and credit. Pay per milestones. Keep signed contracts and call sheets.

title: Selling art through galleries
content: Gallery consignments state commission, insurance, and return with inventory. Photograph works on handover. Keep agreements and inventory.

title: Selling beats exclusively vs non-exclusively
content: Exclusive sales transfer defined rights to one artist; leases allow reuse. Put scope, term, credit, and royalties in writing. Keep licences and payment proof.

title: Beat stolen from YouTube: evidence pack
content: Assemble project files, dated exports, upload logs, messages, and splits before filing takedowns. Preserve message originals. Keep the evidence bundle with dates.

title: Someone copying your brand
content: Collect purchase evidence, report to ACA and KIPI, and send demands before suing. Keep samples, receipts, and registration certificates.

title: Church use of copyrighted music
content: Churches playing or streaming copyrighted music need blanket licences from CMOs. Obtain licences before events. Keep licences and setlists.

title: How long copyright lasts
content: Copyright generally lasts for the author's life plus a statutory period, differing for sound recordings and broadcasts. Confirm the term for the work type. Keep creation and publication records.

title: Answering a counter-notice
content: Counter-notices assert licence or fair use with evidence and consent to process. Respond within deadlines with counsel. Keep licences and correspondence.

title: Cover songs and remixes
content: Covers and remixes need permission from rights holders except as fair dealing allows. Get licences before release. Keep permission letters and licences.

title: Exporting crafts and curios
content: Craft exports need business records, authorised materials, and customs declarations. CITES permits apply to restricted materials. Keep permits and shipping records.

title: Demand letters for infringement
content: Demands identify the work, the infringement, and the remedy with a deadline before suit. Send with evidence annexed. Keep delivery proof and responses.

title: Industrial designs for product look
content: Product shapes and patterns register as industrial designs with novelty requirements. Keep dated drawings and application records.

title: Distributing music on streaming platforms
content: Distributors need accurate splits, ISRC codes, and rights confirmation before release. Verify royalty statements quarterly. Keep distribution contracts and statements.

title: DJ mixtapes and club sets
content: Mixtapes with others tracks need licences for commercial release; venues carry performance licences. Keep licences and tracklists.

title: Domain names and business names
content: Register matching domains early with verified registrars and renew before expiry. Disputes follow registrar policy. Keep registration and renewal records.

title: IP enforcement: demand, KECOBO and courts — general guidance
content: IP disputes often start with a written demand and negotiation, then KECOBO complaints or mediation, then court action for injunctions, damages, or account of profits. Limitation and evidence rules apply, so act early and preserve originals, registrations, and infringement captures with dates.

title: Fair dealing exceptions
content: Research, private study, criticism, and news reporting may use excerpts with attribution within fair limits. Commercial copying rarely qualifies. Get advice before relying on it.

title: Filming permits and locations
citation: Films and Stage Plays Act; KFCB guidance
content: Commercial shoots need KFCB and county permits with location consent. Apply early with scripts and crew lists. Keep permits and consent letters.

title: Franchise agreements
content: Franchises license brands and systems with fees, territories, training, and audit rights. Verify the franchisor record. Keep the agreement and payment records.

title: Freelance creative contracts
content: Freelance briefs state scope, revisions, timelines, fees, and rights transfer with deposits. Keep briefs, drafts, and payment records.

title: KAMP for producers of sound recordings
content: Producers register recordings with KAMP for neighbouring rights collection. Keep master files and registration records.

title: Complaining to KECOBO
content: Complaints attach registration, infringement captures with dates, and demand history. KECOBO may mediate or refer for prosecution. Keep the complaint reference.

title: KFCB classification of films
content: Films for public exhibition need KFCB examination and rating with submission fees. Keep submission receipts and certificates.

title: Legal aid for creators
content: Exploited creators can seek NLAS and KECOBO help with contracts, splits, and registrations. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep all creative records.

title: Logo design ownership
content: Logos transfer only with written assignment; designers retain rights otherwise. Clients secure source files and assignment. Keep design contracts and assignments.

title: MCSK membership for composers
content: Composers and authors join MCSK with IDs, works lists, and fees for royalty collection. Keep membership cards and work declarations.

title: Clearing artist and song names
content: Search KIPI, streaming, and socials for conflicting artist and title names before release. Adjust early. Keep search screenshots.

title: NDAs with staff and partners
content: NDAs define confidential information, duration, and remedies with signatures before disclosure. Keep signed copies and disclosure logs.

title: Using works of unknown owners
content: Document diligent searches for owners before using orphan works, and stop on objection. Keep search records and use logs.

title: Patentability requirements
content: Patents need novelty, inventive step, and industrial application with full disclosure. Public disclosure before filing destroys novelty. Keep lab books confidential.

title: Photography copyright and client use
content: Photographers own images unless assigned in writing; clients get the licensed uses stated. Put deliverables, revisions, and usage in the contract. Keep RAW files and contracts.

title: Book plagiarism and publishing contracts
content: Publishing contracts state royalties, territories, and reversion with manuscript delivery. Register the work with KECOBO. Keep contracts and royalty statements.

title: Poetry and spoken word rights
content: Poems are protected on creation; performances need venue licences and recording consent. Register collections with KECOBO. Keep manuscripts and event records.

title: PRISK for performers
content: Performers register performances with PRISK for broadcast and public-performance royalties. Keep performance records and membership details.

title: Music publishing deals
content: Publishing deals assign administration with advances, splits, and reversion. Compare with CMO collection. Keep deal memos and statements.

title: Getting radio airplay and royalties
content: Submit clean edits with metadata to stations and register works with CMOs for airplay royalties. Track airplay logs. Keep submission and royalty records.

title: Registering copyright step by step
content: Apply to KECOBO with the work copy, applicant IDs, and fees, then collect the certificate. Registration strengthens enforcement. Keep the application, receipt, and certificate.

title: Collecting streaming royalties
content: Register works with MCSK, KAMP, and PRISK as applicable and declare releases for collection. Track statements per work. Keep membership and declaration records.

title: Sampling other recordings
content: Samples need clearance from master and publishing owners with fees. Uncleared samples invite takedowns and suits. Keep clearance letters and payment records.

title: Skiza tunes and caller tunes revenue
content: Skiza deals need written revenue shares, reporting, and audit rights with aggregators. Reconcile statements. Keep contracts and payout records.

title: Stolen social media handles and pages
content: Recover hacked pages through platform verification with IDs and prior admin proof, then report to DCI. Keep admin records and recovery references.

title: Software ownership with developers
content: Code ownership, licences, and escrow belong in written developer contracts with milestones. Keep repositories, contracts, and payment records.

title: Split sheets for collaborations
content: Every session ends with a split sheet naming beatmakers, writers, and percentage shares with signatures. Without it, disputes default to messages. Keep signed splits with project files.

title: Sync licences for adverts and films
content: Sync uses need master and publishing licences with media, term, and fee terms. Clear before broadcast. Keep licences and cue sheets.

title: Filing takedowns that succeed
content: Takedowns need identity, work proof, registration where available, and exact infringing links. File truthfully; false claims attract penalties. Keep case numbers and evidence.

title: Protecting recipes and formulas
content: Guard recipes with NDAs, access controls, and marked confidential documents. Register nothing publicly. Keep signed NDAs and access logs.

title: Filing a trademark at KIPI
content: File with the mark, class, applicant details, and fees, then follow examination and publication. Oppositions have timelines. Keep filing and publication records.

title: Trademark search before branding
content: Search KIPI registers for conflicting marks in the relevant classes before printing packaging. Keep search reports and application receipts.

title: Utility models for smaller inventions
content: Simpler technical improvements may qualify as utility models with shorter terms. File before disclosure. Keep drawings and filing receipts.

title: Videography contracts and footage
content: Video contracts state raw footage ownership, edits, timelines, and payment milestones. Deliver watermarked previews until balance. Keep contracts and delivery logs.

title: KECOBO copyright registration — general guidance
content: Creators can register works with the Kenya Copyright Board for evidence of ownership, increasingly online. Registration supports takedown requests and enforcement. Keep the application, payment receipt, certificate, and the exact files deposited.

title: Stolen beats and songs — general guidance
content: If someone used your beat or song from YouTube without permission, preserve the original project files, timestamps, upload dates, messages, and split sheets showing producers and writers. Options include platform takedown, demand letters, collective management organisations, and KECOBO or court enforcement. Note that beats given away or sold may carry licence terms.

title: Patents, utility models and designs — general guidance
content: Technical inventions, utility models, and industrial designs are registered through the Kenya Industrial Property Institute with novelty and disclosure requirements. Public disclosure before filing can destroy novelty. Keep lab books, drawings, and filing receipts confidential until advised.

title: Trade secrets and confidentiality — general guidance
content: Recipes, client lists, and processes can be protected through confidentiality agreements and access controls rather than registration. Use written non-disclosure terms with staff and partners. Keep signed NDAs and access logs.

title: Trade Marks Act — overview
content: Business names, logos, and slogans can be protected as trademarks through the Kenya Industrial Property Institute, giving exclusive use in registered classes. Registration requires search, application, and publication. Keep search reports, certificates, and use evidence.

title: YouTube and platform takedowns — general guidance
content: Platforms such as YouTube handle copyright complaints with the claimant's details, work proof, and infringing links. File accurately, keep case numbers, and expect counter-notices. False claims carry consequences, so verify ownership and licences first.
